title: Machine learning nominates drug exposures inversely associated with Parkinson risk
summary: LASSO-based screening evaluated historical prescriptions in 40,760 Parkinson cases and 176,395 controls in French health records. Sulfonamide diuretics, especially furosemide, produced the most robust inverse-association signal. Exposure windows preceded diagnosis by years to reduce reverse causation, but confounding and prodromal changes remain possible. These observational hypotheses do not establish prevention, treatment efficacy or a reason to alter medication.
ai_technology: LASSO logistic regression; repeated sample splitting

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective nested case-control screening with 500 repeated split-selection/estimation cycles and sensitivity analyses.
evidence.unknown: Causality, residual confounding, reverse causation and preventive/treatment efficacy remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Cross-validated LASSO selects drug/covariate associations in one half-sample; logistic effects are estimated in the other and aggregated across repeated splits.
